run.request: Our team of six runs everything through email and a shared spreadsheet. We want to move to a shared task tool in two weeks without dropping any client work. Give us a plan for choosing the tool, moving the work over, and getting everyone to actually use it.
run.title: Move your team to a task tool in two weeks
run.goal: Pick a task tool, move client work over and get all six using it.
run.summary: Three people test tools and you pick one by day 3. Everyone moves work on days 4 to 5, runs both systems on days 6 to 8, and cuts over on day 9.

sections.heading: Choose the tool

items: Must-have 1: every task has one owner, one client and a due date.
Must-have 2: a forwarded email becomes a task.
Must-have 3: it imports your spreadsheet as a CSV file.
Cost limit: $15 per person monthly at most, so $90 for six.

body.text: Three people run the trial: the tool owner plus two testers. The other three keep working in email and the spreadsheet, so no client work stalls.

items: Day 1: pick two tools from the table and start free trials.
Day 1: tool owner loads 10 client tasks and 3 forwarded emails into each.
Day 2: the three testers work those tasks in both tools.
Day 3 morning: each tester scores both tools 1 to 5 per must-have.
Day 3 by 5 pm: pick the higher score and buy the plan.

body.text: Top score is 45 per tool. If scores tie, pick the cheaper plan, and do not extend the trial past day 3.
Prices below are estimates, so check the current price page before you buy.

rows: $10 to $25 monthly, often over your cap
Spreadsheet-minded teams, only if a plan fits $15

revised: Steps 3 and 4 say all six test. Schedule says tool owner plus two testers. Use the three testers.
The spreadsheet-style row runs $10 to $25, over the $15 cap. Mark the cap or drop the row.

sections.heading: Move the work

body.text: Clean the spreadsheet before you move anything. Do these steps in order.

items: Copy the spreadsheet and keep that copy untouched as a backup.
Delete finished rows and duplicates so only open client work remains.
Give every row one owner, one client and one due date.
Use one date format everywhere, such as 2026-10-30.
Flag rows missing an owner or date and send them to the tool owner.

body.text: Next, each person turns their own open email threads into tasks.

items: Search your inbox for open client threads from the last 60 days.
Make one task per thread, titled with the next step.
Paste the email subject or link into the task description.
Archive the email only after its task exists in the tool.

body.text: Run both systems on days 6 to 8. Update the tool first, then the sheet.

items: Each afternoon, match open tasks by client and due date.
Fix any gaps that same day.
Day 8: check every open row and thread has a matching task.
Day 9: make the sheet view only. New work goes in the tool.
Keep the backup copy from step 1 for lookups.

revised: Side by side runs days 6 to 9 here. Change it to days 6 to 8 to match the schedule.
Make day 9 the read-only cutover, after a day 8 gap check. Change both the handoff and the body.

body.text: The ten working days run in four stages: choose, set up and move, run side by side, then cut over. Client deadlines come first every day.

items: Day 9 is cutover. The spreadsheet becomes read-only that morning.
Keep moves to about 1 to 2 hours a day per person (estimate).
If a client deadline lands on a move day, move that client last.
If day 8 checks show missing tasks, push cutover one day, not more.

rows: Trial tools, decide end of day 3
Run old and new side by side

items: If a task is not in the tool, it does not exist.
Every task gets one owner and one due date.
A client email asking for work becomes a task the same day.
Discuss work in task comments, not internal email threads.
Check your task list at the start and end of each day.

body.text: Pick one tool owner before day 1, often whoever runs the spreadsheet now. The role takes about 30 to 60 minutes a day (estimate).

items: Meet daily at the same time for 15 minutes, tool on screen.
Each person says what they finished, what is next and what is blocked.
The tool owner flags any task with no owner or due date.
If work still runs through email, put it in the tool then.

body.text: Run the check-in from day 1 through week 3. Hold a 45-minute review on working day 15 using the table below.

rows: Work requests still sent by email
Tasks with no owner or date
Owner assigns them on the spot

next_steps: Name the tool owner and two testers today.
Start two free trials on day 1.
Copy the spreadsheet as a backup before cleaning.
Book the daily 15-minute check-in from day 1.
Put day 9 cutover and day 15 review on calendars.
assumptions: Budget is about $0 to $15 per person monthly.
All six work at least partly online, any location.
Two weeks means ten working days from today.
Client deadlines are fixed and cannot slip.
checks: Schedule fits ten working days and names a cutover day
Includes a side-by-side period so no client task gets lost
Gives a per-person price range, marked as an estimate
Names one owner and clear rules for what stays in email
Steps suit a team of six, not a large company
conflicts: Cutover day: move-work runs both systems on days 6 to 9 and makes the sheet read-only on day 10. two-week-plan runs both on days 6 to 8 and cuts over on day 9.
Trial testers: choose-tool has all six people test on day 2 and score on day 3. two-week-plan lists the tool owner plus two testers for days 1 to 3.
Cost: choose-tool caps cost at $15 per person, but its own table lists spreadsheet-style tools at $10 to $25.
